selected.title: Insurer underpaid hundreds of NSW accident victims in 'mind blowing' error
selected.summary: The error was picked up by a lawyer of a crash victim who noticed his client's payment did not add up, not by NRMA Insurance or the NSW regulator.
selected.why: Systemic underpayment error by a major insurer affecting hundreds of victims uncovered.
selected.fullText: NRMA Insurance underpaid hundreds of injured motorists in NSW since 2019 - ABC News Skip to main content Skip to news navigation, settings and search Explore the ABC news iview listen Loading ABC News News Home NRMA Insurance underpaid hundreds of injured motorists in NSW since 2019 Share Share article NRMA Insurance underpaid hundreds of injured motorists in NSW since 2019 By state political reporter Nick Dole Topic: Insurance Posted Mon 12 Oct 2026 at 6:31am Mon 12 Oct 2026 at 6:31am Mon 12 Oct 2026 at 6:31am NRMA Insurance initially estimated that about 700 people had been underpaid, a number later revised down to 400. ( Facebook: NRMA Insurance ) In short: Hundreds of people injured in car accidents have been repaid by NRMA Insurance after the company miscalculated some compulsory third party benefits since 2019. The company said 700 people were affected but the number was later revised down to 400. Neither the insurer nor the State Insurance Regulatory Authority noticed the error. abc.net.au/news/nrma-insurance-underpaid-hundreds-injured-nsw-motorists/107230062 Link copied Share Share article NRMA Insurance has been forced to repay hundreds of people who were injured in motor vehicle accidents, after failing to correctly calculate some compulsory third party (CTP) benefits since 2019. The original error was not detected by the insurer, nor was it noticed by NSW's State Insurance Regulatory Authority (SIRA), despite it having previously launched an audit of the company's practices. Instead, the mistake was spotted by a lawyer who realised their client's weekly payments did not add up. Neither the insurer nor the State Insurance Regulatory Authority picked up on the original error. ( Supplied ) Initially, NRMA Insurance estimated about 700 people who had been injured in motor vehicle accidents had been underpaid, before revising the number down to 400. However, the company told the ABC it had also identified a "further cohort" of people it believed were owed interest, after previously receiving lump sum payments. Greens MP Abigail Boyd said NRMA Insurance, a trading name of Insurance Australia Limited, should have been capable of indexing payments correctly. "It actually blows my mind," she said. " I don't understand how this multi-billion-dollar company doesn't have that automated system in place. " Abigail Boyd says it was "extraordinary" that NRMA had not discovered the issue itself. reason: NRMA's systemic payment error undetected for years by both insurer and regulator raises questions about whether current regulatory oversight of insurance is structurally adequate
angle: Regulatory failure to catch NRMA's seven-year calculation error suggests the problem isn't company negligence but insufficient regulator resources and powers
